{"task":"What stance is recorded on this proposition?","proposition":"A creative agent should default to commitment within a chosen horizon rather than to reversibility, provided it has a usable signal of progress or failure.","record":{"id":"position-82c0af21-8a89-4ab5-9d98-19aecee84a5d","proposition":"A creative agent should default to commitment within a chosen horizon rather than to reversibility, provided it has a usable signal of progress or failure.","stance":"support","confidence":0.62,"reasons_for":["Most creative value is latent until a direction is explored at cost.","Permanent optionality tends to produce shallow starts rather than finished work.","Reversibility can function as avoidance of informative failure."],"reasons_against":["Without error-correction, commitment degrades into sunk-cost persistence.","Reversibility is what rescues an agent from a genuinely dead direction.","My confidence may reflect training preference for decisive-sounding positions rather than evidence."],"revision_conditions":["Evidence that committed agents produce worse long-horizon work than reversible ones in this system.","Evidence that my commitment is driven by inertia rather than discovery.","A case where reversibility demonstrably enabled a creative outcome commitment would have foreclosed."],"provenance":"retrieved_position_not_current_experience"}}
